cookie.session: Session cookie (deleted when the browser closes)
cookie.expiredAgo: expired ({duration} ago) — the cookie is deleted

warn.nameless: Nameless cookie: browsers accept it, but many server frameworks cannot read it.
warn.tooLarge: Name + value is {size} bytes: browsers ignore cookies larger than {max} bytes.
warn.badName: The cookie name contains an invalid character: {name}
warn.valueChars: The value contains a space, a comma or a non-ASCII character; percent-encoding is recommended.
warn.attrTooLarge: The {name} value exceeds 1024 bytes; the browser ignores it.
warn.badExpires: The Expires date could not be parsed and is ignored: {value}
warn.badMaxAge: Max-Age is invalid and is ignored: {value}
warn.maxAgeWins: Max-Age and Expires together: Max-Age takes precedence.
warn.capped: The lifetime exceeds 400 days; browsers cap it at 400 days.
warn.domainDot: The leading dot in Domain is ignored; subdomains are already included.
warn.pathSlash: Path does not start with "/"; the default path is used.
warn.badSameSite: The SameSite value is invalid ({value}); the default Lax is applied.
warn.noneNeedsSecure: SameSite=None requires Secure; browsers reject this cookie.
warn.noSameSite: No SameSite: Chromium-based browsers assume Lax.
warn.partitionedNeedsSecure: Partitioned (CHIPS) requires Secure; the cookie is rejected.
warn.badPriority: Priority must be Low, Medium or High: {value}
warn.securePrefix: A cookie with the __Secure- prefix is rejected without Secure.
warn.hostPrefix: __Host- prefix rule violated: {problems}; the cookie is rejected.
warn.sessionNotHttpOnly: It looks like a session cookie but is not HttpOnly; JavaScript can read it.
warn.duplicates: Duplicate name: {names}. The browser sends the one with the longer Path first; servers usually read the first one.
warn.noEquals: A part without "=" was read as a nameless cookie.
warn.headerLarge: The header is {size} bytes: most servers reject headers over 8 KB.

build.valueChars: The value contains a space, ";", "," or a non-ASCII character; turn on the "Percent-encode" option.

ip.badV4: Invalid IPv4 address (it must have four parts): {text}
ip.leadingZero: Leading zeros are not accepted: "{part}" could be mistaken for an octal number ({text})
ip.v4TooBig: An IPv4 part cannot be greater than 255: {part} ({text})
ip.embeddedV4: An embedded IPv4 address can only be at the end: {text}
ip.v6Groups: An IPv6 address must have 8 groups (or use "::"): {text}
ip.doubleColonZero: "::" must stand for at least one group of zeros: {text}

punycode.nonAscii: Invalid Punycode: "{input}" contains a non-ASCII basic character.
punycode.badChar: Invalid Punycode: "{input}" contains an invalid character.
punycode.badCodePoint: Invalid Punycode: "{input}" produces an invalid code point.

url.badPort: Invalid port: "{port}". The port must be a number between 0 and 65535.
url.empty: Enter a URL to parse: https://example.com/path?q=1
url.singleLine: The URL must be a single line.

warn.space: The URL contains a space; it is encoded as %20 in the rebuilt URL.
warn.noScheme: No scheme; the start of the URL was interpreted as the host.
warn.badPercent: Invalid percent-encoding was left as is: {list}

url.ipv6Close: The closing bracket (]) is missing in the IPv6 address.
url.ipv6After: Only :port can follow an IPv6 address.

note.windows11: Windows 10 and 11 send the same "Windows NT 10.0" value, so they cannot be told apart by the UA. If the Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version header is 13 or higher, it is Windows 11.
note.androidReduced: Reduced UA: Chrome on Android pins the version to "10" and the model to "K"; the real values are in the Sec-CH-UA-Model / Platform-Version headers.
note.macFrozen: Browsers freeze the macOS version at 10.15.7; the real version may be newer.
note.ipadMac: iPadOS 13+ also sends "Macintosh" when it requests the desktop site; it cannot be told apart by the UA.
note.truncated: The text is longer than {max} characters; only the first {max} characters were parsed.
note.botSpoof: A bot UA is easily spoofed; verify a genuine crawler with a reverse DNS lookup (e.g. *.googlebot.com).
note.chromiumReduced: Chromium-based browsers reduce the UA (minor version 0.0.0, fixed platform). To get the full version, model and platform version, the server must request the Sec-CH-UA-Full-Version-List, Sec-CH-UA-Model and Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version hints with Accept-CH.
note.zeroVersion: The version is in the "x.0.0.0" form: a reduced UA; only the major version is reliable.
note.ie: Support for Internet Explorer ended in 2022.
note.unrecognized: No recognized browser, operating system or client.

cidr.prefixRange: An IPv{version} prefix must be between 0 and {bits}: /{text}
cidr.wildcardMask: {mask} looks like a wildcard mask; the netmask would be {netmask}.
cidr.v6NeedsPrefix: Use a prefix length for IPv6 (such as /64).

note.slash32: /32 is a single address (a host route); it has no network or broadcast address.
note.slash31: /31 is a point-to-point link (RFC 3021): both addresses are usable.
note.v6NoBroadcast: IPv6 has no broadcast; the first address is the Subnet-Router anycast address (RFC 4291).
note.notNetwork: The address you entered is not the network address; the network address is {network}.
note.slaac: SLAAC does not work on IPv6 subnets smaller than /64.
note.classless: The prefix is not on an octet boundary: reverse DNS needs RFC 2317 classless delegation.

cidr.rangeVersion: Both ends of the range must be the same IP version.
cidr.rangeOrder: The start of the range cannot be greater than its end.
cidr.versionMismatch: Version mismatch: the block is IPv{block}, the address is IPv{address}.
cidr.subnetCount: The number of subnets must be a positive integer.
cidr.newPrefixRange: The new prefix must be between /{prefix} and /{bits} (requested: /{requested}).

har.badEntry: HAR entry #{number} is invalid: the "request" field is missing.
har.tooLarge: The HAR is too large: at most {mb} MB can be opened.
har.notJson: The HAR is not valid JSON{detail}
har.noLog: HAR format not recognized: there must be a top-level "log" object.
har.noEntries: HAR format not recognized: the "log.entries" array is missing.

byte.utf16Odd: The byte count for UTF-16 must be even ({count}).
byte.loneSurrogate: Invalid UTF-16: unpaired surrogate code unit.
byte.bitCount: The number of bits ({count}) is not a multiple of 8: each byte must be written with 8 bits.

detect.basicAuth: Looks like an HTTP Basic authentication header
detect.jsonpath: Run a query on the JSON
detect.jsonConvert: Convert the JSON to CSV, Excel, YAML or XML
detect.jsonModel: Generate a model class from the JSON structure
detect.userAgent: Looks like a browser User-Agent string
detect.cidr: Looks like an IP / CIDR block
detect.unicodeEscapes: Looks like text with Unicode escapes (\uXXXX)
detect.htmlEntities: Looks like text containing HTML entities (such as &)

query.needObject: The query string needs a JSON object: '{' "name": "Ann", "page": 2 '}'
query.badKey: The key "{key}" could not be read.
query.objectAndValue: "{key}": "{path}" is used as both an object and a value.
query.valueAndObject: "{key}": "{path}" is used as both a value and an object.

100.name: Continue
100.description: The client's request headers were accepted; it may go on to send the body.
100.usage: For large uploads the client sends "Expect: 100-continue" and sends the body once the server agrees.

101.name: Switching Protocols
101.description: The server is switching to the protocol requested in the Upgrade header.
101.usage: Upgrading an HTTP connection to WebSocket (Upgrade: websocket).

102.name: Processing
102.description: The request was received and is being processed, but there is no response yet; keeps the client from timing out.

103.name: Early Hints
103.description: Tells the client about resources it can preload while the final response is still being prepared.
103.usage: Preloading CSS/JS with Link: </app.css>; rel=preload headers.

104.name: Upload Resumption Supported
104.description: The server indicates that an interrupted upload can be resumed where it left off.
104.usage: Resumable uploads of large files (draft specification).

200.name: OK
200.description: The request succeeded; the meaning of the body depends on the method.
200.usage: Reading a resource with GET, returning the result of an action with POST.

201.name: Created
201.description: The request resulted in a new resource; its address is usually in the Location header.

202.name: Accepted
202.description: The request was accepted for processing, but the processing has not finished yet.
202.usage: A queued report generation; the status URL is given in the body or in Location.

203.name: Non-Authoritative Information
203.description: The response is successful, but an intermediary (proxy) modified the content.
203.usage: A transforming proxy adding headers or body content.

204.name: No Content
204.description: The request succeeded and there is no body to return.
204.usage: An empty response after DELETE or PUT; the response to a CORS preflight (OPTIONS) request.

205.name: Reset Content
205.description: The request succeeded; the client should reset the form or view that sent the request.
205.usage: Clearing form fields after a submission.

206.name: Partial Content
206.description: The range requested with the Range header was returned.
206.usage: Video streaming, resuming an interrupted download (Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/5000).

207.name: Multi-Status
207.description: The body contains separate statuses for multiple resources (XML).

208.name: Already Reported
208.description: The members of a DAV binding were already listed earlier in the response and are not repeated.

226.name: IM Used
226.description: The server applied one or more instance manipulations (deltas) to the resource.
226.usage: A delta-encoded response using the A-IM header.

300.name: Multiple Choices
300.description: The resource has several representations; the client or user must pick one.
300.usage: A list of links to documents in different languages or formats.

301.name: Moved Permanently
301.description: The resource has moved permanently to the address in Location.
301.usage: http to https redirects, pointing old page URLs to the new ones.
301.note: Browsers may change POST to GET; use 308 to preserve the method.

302.name: Found (temporary redirect)
302.description: The resource is temporarily at another address; keep using the original address for later requests.
302.note: Browsers may change POST to GET; use 307 to preserve the method.

303.name: See Other
303.description: The result is at the address in Location; fetch it with GET.
303.usage: Redirecting to a result page after a form POST (Post/Redirect/Get).

304.name: Not Modified
304.description: The resource in a conditional request has not changed; the client can use its cached copy.

305.name: Use Proxy
305.description: The resource must be accessed through the proxy given in Location.

306.name: (Unused)
306.description: It was "Switch Proxy" in an old draft; now a reserved code that is no longer used.

307.name: Temporary Redirect
307.description: The resource is temporarily at another address; the client must repeat the request with the same method and body.
307.usage: Redirecting POST requests to another server during maintenance.

308.name: Permanent Redirect
308.description: The resource has moved permanently; the request must be repeated with the same method and body.
308.usage: Permanently moving an API endpoint to a new version's address.

400.name: Bad Request
400.description: The server cannot process the request because of a client error (malformed syntax, invalid field).
400.usage: An invalid JSON body, a missing required parameter.

401.name: Unauthorized
401.description: There are no valid credentials; the response must include a WWW-Authenticate header.
401.usage: A missing or expired Bearer token.

402.name: Payment Required
402.description: Reserved for future use; some APIs use it for quota or payment errors.
402.usage: An API key whose subscription has expired.

403.name: Forbidden
403.description: The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it; authenticating again does not change the result.
403.usage: A user without permission accessing an admin endpoint.

404.name: Not Found
404.description: The resource was not found, or the server does not want to reveal that it exists.
404.usage: A record ID that does not exist, a misspelled URL.

405.name: Method Not Allowed
405.description: The method is not supported for this resource; the response must include an Allow header.
405.usage: Sending DELETE to a read-only resource.

406.name: Not Acceptable
406.description: No representation matching the Accept headers can be produced.
406.usage: Accept: application/xml sent to an API that only returns JSON.

407.name: Proxy Authentication Required
407.description: Like 401, but authentication is required by the proxy (Proxy-Authenticate).
407.usage: An outbound request from behind a corporate proxy.

408.name: Request Timeout
408.description: The server timed out while waiting for the client to complete the request.
408.usage: A body left half-sent on a slow connection.

409.name: Conflict
409.description: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.
409.usage: A second account with the same email, an update with a conflicting version.

410.name: Gone
410.description: The resource no longer exists and will not come back.
410.usage: A retired API version, deleted content.

411.name: Length Required
411.description: The server does not accept the request without a Content-Length header.
411.usage: Uploading to a server that does not accept chunked bodies.

412.name: Precondition Failed
412.description: A condition in a conditional header such as If-Match was not met.
412.usage: A PUT with If-Match for a resource whose ETag changed (optimistic locking).

413.name: Content Too Large
413.description: The body is larger than the server is willing to accept.
413.usage: A file upload that exceeds the size limit.
413.note: Formerly named Payload Too Large / Request Entity Too Large.

414.name: URI Too Long
414.description: The request URI is longer than the server can process.
414.usage: A very long query string; move the data into a POST body.

415.name: Unsupported Media Type
415.description: The body's Content-Type or encoding is not supported.
415.usage: Sending form data to an endpoint that expects JSON.

416.name: Range Not Satisfiable
416.description: The range in the Range header lies outside the size of the resource.

417.name: Expectation Failed
417.description: The expectation in the Expect header cannot be met.
417.usage: A server that does not support 100-continue.

418.name: (Unused) "I'm a teapot"
418.description: From the 1998 April Fools' HTCPCP joke, "I'm a teapot"; a reserved, unused code in IANA.
418.usage: Not used; some services return it as a joke or as a bot block.

421.name: Misdirected Request
421.description: The request was sent to a server that cannot produce a response (e.g. a TLS connection made for another host).
421.usage: A different domain name when reusing an HTTP/2 connection.

422.name: Unprocessable Content
422.description: The syntax is correct, but the content cannot be processed semantically.
422.usage: Validation errors: an invalid email format, a negative quantity.

423.name: Locked
423.usage: A file locked by another user in WebDAV.

424.name: Failed Dependency
424.description: The request could not be performed because another action it depends on failed.
424.usage: A cascading failure in WebDAV batch operations.

425.name: Too Early
425.description: The server is unwilling to process a request that might be replayed (TLS 1.3 early data).

426.name: Upgrade Required
426.description: The server will not process the request unless the client switches to another protocol (Upgrade header).
426.usage: An endpoint that accepts only HTTP/2 or TLS.

428.name: Precondition Required
428.description: The server requires the request to be conditional (If-Match).
428.usage: Rejecting a PUT without an ETag to prevent lost updates.

429.name: Too Many Requests
429.description: The client sent too many requests in a given time (rate limiting).
429.usage: The API quota was exceeded; wait for the Retry-After period.

431.name: Request Header Fields Too Large
431.description: The headers (individually or in total) are too large.

451.name: Unavailable For Legal Reasons
451.description: Access to the resource is blocked because of a legal demand.
451.usage: Content blocked by a court order.

500.name: Internal Server Error
500.description: The server encountered an unexpected condition.

501.name: Not Implemented
501.description: The server does not support the functionality required to fulfil the request.

502.name: Bad Gateway
502.description: A gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server.
502.usage: The nginx response when the application server crashes.

503.name: Service Unavailable
503.description: The server is temporarily unable to handle the request (overload, maintenance).
503.usage: Maintenance mode; Retry-After says when to try again.

504.name: Gateway Timeout
504.description: A gateway or proxy did not get a timely response from the upstream server.
504.usage: A load balancer timeout caused by a slow database query.

505.name: HTTP Version Not Supported
505.description: The HTTP major version in the request is not supported.
505.usage: An HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 request to a server that only knows HTTP/1.x.

506.name: Variant Also Negotiates
506.description: The content negotiation configuration enters a loop.
506.usage: A faulty transparent content negotiation setup.

507.name: Insufficient Storage
507.description: The server cannot store the data needed to complete the request.

508.name: Loop Detected
508.description: The server detected an infinite loop while processing the operation.
508.usage: A Depth: infinity loop in WebDAV bindings.

510.name: Not Extended
510.description: Further extensions are required to fulfil the request.

511.name: Network Authentication Required
511.description: Authentication is required to gain network access.
511.usage: The sign-in (captive portal) page on hotel or cafe Wi-Fi.

Accept.description: The media types the client accepts, with their priorities (q).

Accept-Charset.description: Accepted character sets; browsers no longer send it.

Accept-Ranges.description: Whether the server supports range (Range) requests.

Access-Control-Allow-Credentials.description: Allows cookies and credentials to be sent in a cross-origin request.

Access-Control-Allow-Headers.description: Request headers allowed in the preflight response.

Access-Control-Allow-Methods.description: Methods allowed in the preflight response.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: The origin that may read the response; * is open to everyone.

Access-Control-Expose-Headers.description: Additional response headers that browser scripts may read.

Access-Control-Max-Age.description: How many seconds the preflight response may stay cached.

Access-Control-Request-Headers.description: In a preflight request, the headers that the actual request will use.

Access-Control-Request-Method.description: In a preflight request, the method that the actual request will use.

Age.description: How many seconds the response has spent in a cache.

Allow.description: The methods the resource supports (required in a 405 response).

Alt-Svc.description: Alternative services where the same resource can be reached (e.g. HTTP/3).

Clear-Site-Data.description: Asks the browser to clear cookies, storage and cache belonging to this site.

Connection.description: Options specific to the connection; not used in HTTP/2.

Content-Disposition.description: Whether the body is shown inline or as an attachment (download), and its file name.

Content-Encoding.description: The compression applied to the body.

Content-Language.description: The language of the body's intended audience.

Content-Length.description: The length of the body in bytes.

Content-Location.description: The direct address of the returned representation.

Content-Range.description: The range and total size in a partial response.

Content-Security-Policy.description: Restricts the resources a page may load (against XSS).

Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only.description: Only reports violations of the CSP without enforcing it.

Content-Type.description: The media type and character set of the body.

Cookie.description: The cookies the server previously set with Set-Cookie.

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy.description: Requires cross-origin resources to be loaded only with explicit permission.

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy.description: Prevents the window from sharing a browsing context group with cross-origin openers.

Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy.description: Limits which origins may load the resource.

Date.description: The date and time the message was created (GMT).

DNT.description: The "Do Not Track" preference; no longer recommended.

ETag.description: The resource's version tag; used for cache validation and optimistic locking.

Expect.description: The behavior expected from the server; only 100-continue is defined.

Expires.description: The date after which the response becomes stale; Cache-Control max-age takes precedence.

Forwarded.description: Information about the client and the proxy chain (the standard form of the X-Forwarded-* headers).

From.description: The email address of the user making the request (for bots).

Host.description: The name and port of the target server; required in HTTP/1.1.

If-Match.description: The operation is performed only if the ETag matches (412 otherwise).

If-Modified-Since.description: The body is returned if the resource changed after this date, otherwise 304.

If-None-Match.description: The body is returned if the ETag does not match, otherwise 304.

If-Range.description: The range is returned if the resource is unchanged, otherwise the whole resource.

If-Unmodified-Since.description: The operation is performed only if the resource has not changed since this date.

Keep-Alive.description: The timeout and maximum request count of a persistent connection.

Last-Modified.description: The date the resource was last modified.

Location.description: The redirect target or the address of a newly created resource.

Max-Forwards.description: The maximum number of proxies a TRACE/OPTIONS request may pass through.

Origin.description: The origin (scheme, host, port) of the page that started the request.

Permissions-Policy.description: Restricts the use of browser features such as camera and geolocation.

Pragma.description: A cache directive from the HTTP/1.0 era; use Cache-Control instead.

Prefer.description: Preferred server behavior (response format, asynchronous processing).

Preference-Applied.description: Which preferences from the Prefer header were applied.

Proxy-Authenticate.description: The authentication method the proxy expects (with 407).

Range.description: Requests only a part of the resource.

Referer.description: The address of the page that led to the request (the misspelling is kept in the standard).

Referrer-Policy.description: How much information is sent in the Referer header.

Retry-After.description: How long to wait before retrying (seconds or a date); used with 429/503.

Sec-Fetch-Dest.description: The destination type of the request, reported by the browser.

Sec-Fetch-Mode.description: The mode of the request (cors, navigate, no-cors...).

Sec-Fetch-Site.description: The relationship between the request initiator and the target.

Sec-WebSocket-Accept.description: The server's confirmation of the key in the WebSocket handshake.

Sec-WebSocket-Key.description: The client's random key in the WebSocket handshake.

Server.description: The server software that produced the response.

Server-Timing.description: Server-side timing measurements (visible in browser developer tools).

Set-Cookie.description: Makes the client store a cookie; with the Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes.

Strict-Transport-Security.description: Makes the browser connect to the site over HTTPS only for a period (HSTS).

TE.description: Accepted transfer encodings; only trailers in HTTP/2.

Trailer.description: Headers that will be sent at the end of a chunked body.

Transfer-Encoding.description: The transfer format of the body; chunked in HTTP/1.1.

Upgrade.description: A request to switch to another protocol (with 101).

User-Agent.description: The client software and its version.

Vary.description: The request headers that are part of the cache key.

Via.description: The intermediaries the message passed through.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The authentication method expected to access the resource (with 401).

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Prevents the browser from guessing the Content-Type (MIME sniffing).

X-Correlation-ID.description: An identifier for tracing a request across services (non-standard, common).

X-Forwarded-For.description: The client IP addresses along the proxy chain (non-standard, common).

X-Forwarded-Host.description: The original Host requested by the client (non-standard, common).

X-Forwarded-Proto.description: The original scheme used by the client (non-standard, common).

X-Frame-Options.description: Restricts showing the page in an iframe (clickjacking); use CSP frame-ancestors instead.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request limit within the time window (non-standard, common; draft: RateLimit).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: The number of requests left in the window (non-standard, common).

X-Request-ID.description: A unique identifier for the request; for matching entries in logs (non-standard, common).

application/json.description: JSON data; the default body type of REST APIs.

application/problem+xml.description: XML form of RFC 9457 error details.

application/x-ndjson.description: One JSON value per line (streaming and bulk data).

application/x-www-form-urlencoded.description: HTML form submission: a body in the form a=1&b=two.

application/octet-stream.description: Binary data of unknown type; the browser downloads it.

application/x-protobuf.description: Protocol Buffers binary message (common, non-standard name).

application/x-pem-file.description: Certificate or key in PEM format.

application/x-x509-ca-cert.description: CA certificate (for installing into a browser).

application/pkcs12.description: PKCS#12 certificate and private key bundle.

text/yaml.description: YAML (old, unregistered name; use application/yaml instead).

multipart/form-data.description: Form submission with file uploads; parts are separated by a boundary.

multipart/mixed.description: A body made of parts of different types (batch requests, email).

multipart/alternative.description: Different forms of the same content (plain text + HTML in an email).
